decisive_spans.text: cyanotic after an episode of severe cough and hemoptysis (approximately 50ml in volume) following a severe cold leading to pneumonia in July 2016
Revealed a patent foramen ovale measuring 7.34 mm in width with a continuous, pure right-to-left shunt on colour flow mapping

response.rationale: The patient's history of progressive cyanosis, recurrent chest pain and shortness of breath, along with echocardiographic evidence of a right-to-left shunt through a patent foramen ovale, strongly supports Eisenmenger Syndrome. Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal is a broader category that includes Eisenmenger Syndrome, but the specific findings point to the latter. Pulmonary Hypertension is present but is a component of Eisenmenger Syndrome, not the primary diagnosis. Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension is ruled out by pulmonary angiography.
